text: You could count every cookie.
That works. But it's slow, and it's easy to lose your place.
Is there a faster way? Yes. Look at the plates.
When every group has the same number, you can count a whole group at a time.
Look. Each plate is a group.
There are 4 plates, so there are 4 groups.
And each plate has 3 cookies. That's 3 in each group.
Now count one whole plate at a time.
So there are 12 cookies.
4 groups of 3 make 12.
We write that as 4 times 3 equals 12.
The first number is the groups. The second is how many in each.
Here's the part people mix up.

text: Each row has 5 chairs.

What does fair mean here?
If one friend gets 6 and another gets 2, that isn't fair.
Every friend must get the same number.
Division shares a total into equal groups, and here we know how many groups, so we find how many in each.

Then go round again. Now each friend has 2.

Now count the first friend's apples. One, two, three, four.

12 shared by 3 friends is 4 each.
We write 12 divided by 3 equals 4.

Tidy it up, 3 a plus 20 equals 32. Take 20 off both sides, and 3 a equals 12.

Look at this table.
You might hunt for a pattern, like outputs that go up.
There isn't one. 5, 2, 9, 2.
So is this table broken? No. The real question is much simpler than a pattern.
A function gives each input exactly one output, so one input with two different outputs breaks it.
Walk the inputs one at a time.
Input 1 gives 3. Input 2 gives 5.
Input 3 gives 7, and input 4 gives 9.
Every input shows up once, with one output. So this table is a function.
Now watch this one.
Input 2 shows up twice.
Once it gives 6, and once it gives 8.
That is button A giving chips today and a cookie tomorrow. Not a function.
Here is one that looks strange. Every input gives 5.
Is that allowed? Yes. Two buttons can give you the same snack.
Each input still has just one output, so this is a function.
Don't call it not a function just because an output repeats.
Only one input with two different outputs breaks the rule.
You drop in 4. Can you just look and know what comes out?
No. The machine does not guess, and neither can you.
You have to follow its rule, step by step, in the right order.
Put the input into the rule, then multiply before you add or subtract, and that gives the output.
Our input is 4.
So wherever the rule says input, we write a 4 instead.
That gives us 3 times 4 minus 2.
Which comes first, the times or the minus?
Multiply first. 3 times 4 equals 12.
Then take away the 2. 12 minus 2 equals 10.
So when 4 goes in, 10 comes out.
People write this same rule a shorter way.
It looks like f of x equals 3 x minus 2.
The x is the input, and 3 x means 3 times x.
So f of 4 asks for the output when 4 goes in, and we already found it, 10.
Don't subtract before you multiply.
3 times 4 minus 2 is not 3 times 2. Multiply 3 times 4 first, then take away the 2.
Look at both tables.
Plant A gets taller every week. So does Plant B.
So does going up tell them apart? No.
What matters is how much each one grows every week.
When x goes up in equal steps and y changes by the same amount every step, the points make a straight line.
Start with Plant A. Each week, x goes up 1.
The height goes 1, 3, 5, 7.
That is up 2, up 2, up 2, the same step every time.
Plot those points, and they sit on one straight line.
Now Plant B. It goes 0, 1, 4, 9.
Is that the same step each week? No.
It goes up 1, then up 3, then up 5, so the points bend upward.
Plant A grew by the same amount every week, so its points make a straight line.
A table like that has a name.
We call it linear. Plant B is not linear.
Don't compare the y changes before you check the x steps.
If x goes up 1 and then up 2, y should go up twice as far the second time. That is still a straight line.
Look. One is a table, and one is a rule.
Ava starts with 10 dollars, and Ben starts with only 2 dollars.
Does that mean Ava grows faster? Not yet. Where you start is not how fast you grow.
For each one, find how much it goes up for every 1 step in x, and the bigger number grows faster.
Take Ava first. Her savings go 10, 16, 22, 28, one week at a time.
How much is each step? 16 minus 10 equals 6, and every step is 6.
So Ava goes up 6 dollars a week.
Now Ben. His rule is y equals 8 x plus 2.
Try weeks 0, 1 and 2. He has 2 dollars, then 10 dollars, then 18 dollars.
Each week adds 8 more, the same 8 that sits in front of x.
So Ben goes up 8 dollars a week.
Now put the two side by side. Ava goes up 6 a week, and Ben goes up 8.
Which is bigger? 8 is more than 6.
So Ben grows faster, even though Ava started with more.
Don't pick the one that starts higher.
The plus 2 in Ben's rule is where he starts. The 8 in front of x is how fast he grows.

The amount that repeats goes in front of x, and the amount paid once is added on.

So at 0 months, before any month has gone by, you have already paid 25 dollars.
Now the part that repeats. Every month adds another 10 dollars.
So x months add 10 times x, and we write that as 10 x.
Does it work? Try 3 months. 10 times 3 equals 30, and 30 plus 25 equals 55.
Now put the two pieces together. The cost is 10 times the months, plus 25.
With y for the cost and x for the months, that is y equals 10 x plus 25.
And 24 months? 10 times 24 plus 25 equals 265. One line, and it is done.
Don't multiply the 25 dollars by the months.
You pay the 25 dollars once, so it is added on. The 10 dollars is what repeats, so 10 goes in front of x.
There is no rule here to put numbers into.
So how can a graph tell a story?
You read its shape, one piece at a time.
Read the graph from left to right, where up means growing, down means shrinking, and flat means staying the same.
Start at the left. From hour 0 to hour 2, the graph climbs to 6 miles.
What does that mean for Sam?
His distance from home is growing, so he is riding away.
Next piece. From hour 2 to hour 4, the graph stays flat at 6 miles.
Is Sam getting any farther from home? No.
His distance is not changing, so he has stopped for a rest.
From hour 4 to hour 6 it climbs again, but only 2 miles.
From hour 0 to hour 2 it climbed 6. Steeper means faster.
Then from hour 6 to hour 10 it goes down to 0, because Sam is riding home.
The graph is not a picture of a hill.
Going down does not mean Sam rides downhill. It means he is getting closer to home.
You could just drag it across and hope it lands right.
But where exactly does it land? Hoping can't tell you.
You need the new spot of every single corner.
In a slide, every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
Take corner A. It starts at 1, 1.
Move it 4 to the right, and x goes from 1 up to 5.
Move it 2 up, and y goes from 1 up to 3.
So A lands on 5, 3. We call that new point A prime.
The other two corners do the same thing.
B at 3, 1 goes to 7, 3. C at 1, 3 goes to 5, 5.
Every corner went 4 right and 2 up.
Nothing stretched and nothing turned, so it is the same triangle, just moved.
Is there a rule that works for every point? Yes.
Right adds to x, and left takes away from x.
Up adds to y, and down takes away from y.
So for 4 right and 2 up, every point x, y becomes x plus 4, y plus 2.
Don't add the right move to y. Right and left change x, the first number.
Up and down change y, the second one.
So 4 right and 2 up takes 1, 1 to 5, 3. Not to 3, 5.
Could we just slide the triangle straight down?
Look. It comes out the same way up.
But the picture in the water is upside down, so a slide can't make it.
Flip over the x-axis and the y changes sign, flip over the y-axis and the x changes sign.
Look at corner A, at 2, 1. It sits 1 square above the x-axis.
Its picture sits 1 square below, straight down. Same distance, other side.
So A at 2, 1 becomes A prime at 2, negative 1.
The other corners do the same.
B at 4, 1 drops to 4, negative 1. C at 2, 3 drops to 2, negative 3.
Look down the list. Every x stayed the same, and every y flipped its sign.
Now flip the same triangle the other way, over the y-axis.
It swings across to the left. A at 2, 1 lands on negative 2, 1.
This time y stays put, and it is x that changes sign.
A flip over the x-axis does not change x.
The point moves straight down, so only the y changes.
So 2, 1 becomes 2, negative 1, not negative 2, 1.
Can we just count squares, like a slide?
No. Each corner swings around the point 0, 0 on its own circle.
A corner far from the center travels farther than a close one, so no single count works.
A quarter turn counterclockwise around the point 0, 0 sends x, y to negative y, x.
Follow corner A, at 3, 1. That is 3 right and 1 up from the center.
Turn that arm a quarter turn, the way a clock hand goes backward.
Now it points 1 left and 3 up. So A prime is at negative 1, 3.
Look at what happened to the numbers.
They swapped places, and then the new first number changed sign.
Check B. 4, 1 swaps to 1, 4, and the sign change gives negative 1, 4.
C at 3, 3 goes to negative 3, 3. Same rule.
Now turn twice as far, until the board faces the other way.
That is a half turn, 180 degrees.
Nothing swaps this time. Both signs change.
So A at 3, 1 goes to negative 3, negative 1.
Don't just swap the numbers and stop.
A swap is only half the job.
Change the sign of the new first number, so 3, 1 goes to negative 1, 3.
What if we just add 2 to every number?
Look. The triangle only slides over. It is the same size as before.
But we want every side twice as long.
To stretch a shape from the point 0, 0, multiply both coordinates of every point by the same number.
Start with corner A, at 2, 1.
Multiply both numbers by 2, and you get 4, 2.
A prime lands on the same straight line out from the point 0, 0, just twice as far along it.
Do the same to the other two.
B at 4, 1 doubles to 8, 2. C at 2, 3 doubles to 4, 6.
Now measure a side. The bottom was 2 squares long, and now it is 4.
Every side is twice as long.
Can the same move shrink a shape? Yes.
Multiply by one half, and 8, 2 goes right back to 4, 1.
A number bigger than 1 grows the shape. A number smaller than 1 shrinks it.
Twice as big does not mean add 2.
Adding 2 to 2, 1 gives 4, 3, and that only slides it.
Multiply both numbers, so 2, 1 becomes 4, 2.
Did every side just grow by the same amount? Let's test it.
The bottom went from 4 to 8. That is 4 more.
But the 3 foot side went to 6, and that is only 3 more.
Different amounts, so adding is not what happened.
Triangles with the same angles have every side multiplied by the same number.
Look at the corners first, not the sides.
Each corner of the big sign has the same angle as a corner of the small one.
So each big side matches the small side in the same place.
Pick a pair where you know both sides, the bottoms, 4 and 8.
8 divided by 4 equals 2, so the big side is 2 times as long.
Check a second pair. 3 times 2 equals 6, and the big sign says 6.
Now the side we came for.
It matches the 2 foot side on the small sign.
So 2 times 2 equals 4. The missing side is 4 feet.
Don't add the difference you saw.
2 plus 4 equals 6 feet gives a sign with a different shape.
Multiply by 2 every time, so 2 times 2 equals 4 feet.

The three angles inside a triangle always add to 180 degrees, so the angle outside a corner equals the two far inside angles added.
Here is something you can try with paper.
Tear the three corners off a paper triangle, then push their points together.
They line up. Every time, they make one straight line, and a straight line is 180 degrees.
So back to the roof. Add the two angles you know, 50 plus 60 equals 110.
How much is left over out of 180? 180 minus 110 equals 70.
The top angle is 70 degrees.
Now stretch the bottom side out past the 60 degree corner.
The angle that opens up outside is 180 minus 60 equals 120 degrees.
Look. That is exactly the two far angles added together, 50 plus 70 equals 120.
Don't stop at 50 plus 60 equals 110.
That is two angles together, not the third one. Take it away from 180 degrees, and you get 70 degrees.

Now tip those two squares into the big one on the long side.

5 times 5 equals 25.

When you already know the long side, take the short side's square away from the long side's square, then undo the square.
Build the squares again, the same way as before.
The square on the 5 meter ladder holds 5 times 5 equals 25. The square on the 3 meter ground holds 3 times 3 equals 9.
The square on the wall is the one we are hunting for.
The two small squares fill the big one exactly.

25 minus 9 equals 16.

It is a square corner, so what you have drawn is a right triangle.

In a box, you could stack little cubes and just count them.
A can is round, though.
Push cubes against the curved side, and you get gaps.
So how do you measure a space that is round?
A cylinder is a stack of circles, so find the area of one circle and multiply by the height.
Start with the circle on the bottom.
From the center to the edge is 2 inches, so the radius is 2.
The area of a circle is three point one four times the radius times the radius.
Three point one four times 2 times 2 is twelve point five six square inches, one flat layer.
Now stack that circle up the can.
Each inch of height adds a layer of twelve point five six.
How many layers fit? The can is 5 inches tall, so 5 layers.
One layer is twelve point five six. We want 5.
Twelve point five six times 5 is sixty-two point eight.
In one go, that is three point one four times 2 times 2 times 5, the circle, then the height.
So your can holds sixty-two point eight cubic inches of soup.
Don't use the distance all the way across.
This can is 4 inches across, but the rule wants the radius, half of that, 2 inches.
Look down this cup from the top.
Its circles get smaller and smaller, until they shrink to a point.
So can you stack one circle, like in a can? No.
Every layer is a different size.
A cone holds one third of the cylinder with the same bottom and height, so find the cylinder and divide by 3.
Try this for real.
Fill the cone with water, and pour it into a cylinder with the same bottom and height.
How full is the cylinder after one pour? Only a third.
It takes 3 whole cones to fill it.
So forget the cone for a moment.
Build the cylinder with the same bottom and height.
The circle is three point one four times 3 times 3, and the height is 4.
Three point one four times 3 times 3 times 4 is one hundred thirteen point zero four cubic centimeters.
Now bring the cone back.
It holds one third of what that cylinder holds.
So we divide by 3. One hundred thirteen point zero four divided by 3 is thirty-seven point six eight.
Your paper cup holds thirty-seven point six eight cubic centimeters of water.
Don't stop once you have the cylinder.
A cone holds only one third of it, so divide by 3 at the end.
A ball has no flat bottom and no straight height.

Its radius is the same as the ball's, 3 inches.
And how tall is it? The whole way across the ball, so 3 times 2 equals 6 inches.
Fill the can with water, then push the ball in.
The water that spills out is as big as the ball.
How much spills? Two thirds of the can. One third stays in.
The can first. Three point one four times 3 times 3 times 6 equals one hundred sixty-nine point five six.
The ball is two thirds of that. One hundred sixty-nine point five six, divided by 3, times 2, equals one hundred thirteen point zero four.
Is there a faster way? Yes. Four thirds times three point one four times 3 times 3 times 3 gives the same one hundred thirteen point zero four.
So the ball holds one hundred thirteen point zero four cubic inches.
Don't use the radius only twice, the way you would for a flat circle.
A ball is round every way, so the radius goes in three times.

The scoop on top is half of a ball.

It is one third of a can with the same bottom and the same height.

Now the scoop. Find a whole ball first.
Four thirds times three point one four times 3 times 3 times 3 equals one hundred thirteen point zero four.
But only half a ball sits on top, so halve it.
One hundred thirteen point zero four, divided by 2, equals fifty-six point five two.
Two pieces, two numbers.
Thirty-seven point six eight from the cone, and fifty-six point five two from the scoop.
Add them. Thirty-seven point six eight plus fifty-six point five two equals ninety-four point two.

Don't add a whole ball when only half of one sits on top.
Halve it first, then add. Thirty-seven point six eight plus fifty-six point five two equals ninety-four point two.

So how many grade 7 students like pizza? Those two counts cannot tell you.
Put one question in the rows and one in the columns, so each box counts the people who fit both.
Let's fill one box together.
12 students are in grade 7 and they like pizza.
Where does that 12 go? Right where the Grade 7 row meets the Likes pizza column.
Now check each row. It has to add up to its own total.

In grade 8, 15 and 5 make 20 as well.

Don't add a row total to a column total.

Now we divide by the Likes pizza column total, 27.

Now you try. You guess a jar holds 68 marbles. The real count is 80. By what percent was your guess off? Find the gap. Divide it by the real count, then multiply by 100.
Now you try. What is the opposite of negative 6? Count the steps from 0. Go the same distance on the other side.
Now you try. How far is negative 8 from 0? Count the steps from the number to 0. Drop the sign.
Now you try. Add. 4 plus negative 7 equals what? Pair each plus with a minus. Take the pairs away. Count what is left.
Now you try. Take away. negative 1 minus 6 equals what? Change minus to plus and use the opposite. Then move on the line.
Now you try. Multiply. Negative 4 times negative 3 equals what? Multiply without the signs. Then check, same signs or different?
Now you try. Divide. Negative 20 divided by negative 5 equals what? Divide without the signs. Then check, same signs or different?
Now you try. Add. Negative one fourth plus three fourths equals what? Keep the minus sign. Start at the first number and jump on the line.

Now you try. It is negative 4 degrees Celsius in the morning. By the afternoon it is 9 degrees warmer. What is the temperature in the afternoon, in degrees Celsius? Let the words pick the sign. Then climb the thermometer.
Now you try. Which is the same as 4 x plus 2 plus 3 x plus 6? Put the x parts together. Then put the plain numbers together.
Now you try. Which is the same as negative 3 times x minus 5, all together? Multiply the number outside by every part inside. Watch the signs.
Now you try. Which is the same as 8 x plus 12? Find the biggest number that divides every part. Put it outside.
Now you try. Solve 3 x plus 5 equals 20. What is x? Undo the adding first. Then undo the multiplying.
Now you try. Solve 4 times x plus 3, all together, equals 32. What is x? Divide both sides by the number outside. Then solve what is left.
Now you try. Solve 3 x plus 2 is greater than 14. Which is the answer? Solve it like an equation. Keep the sign.
Now you try. Solve negative 2 x is less than 10. Which is the answer? Divide both sides. If you divide by a negative, flip the sign.

Now you try. A gym costs 15 dollars to join, plus 8 dollars for each class. Leo paid 63 dollars. How many classes did he take? Use a letter for what you do not know. Write the equation, then solve it.

Now you try. On a map, 1 centimeter equals 50 meters. A road is 8 centimeters long on the map. How many meters long is the real road? Find what 1 centimeter stands for. Then multiply by the map length.
Now you try. A plate has a diameter of 20 centimeters. How far is it around the edge, in centimeters? Use three point one four. Multiply the distance across by three point one four.
Now you try. A round rug has a radius of 3 meters. What is its area in square meters? Use pi as three point one four. Multiply the radius by itself. Then multiply by three point one four.
Now you try. Two angles make a square corner. One is 28 degrees. How many degrees is the other? Find the whole first. Then take away the angle you know.
Now you try. Two straight lines cross. One angle is 65 degrees. What is the angle straight across from it? Is the missing angle straight across, or next door?
Now you try. Can sticks 2 centimeters, 5 centimeters and 8 centimeters long make a triangle? Add the two shorter sides. Is that more than the longest?

Now you try. A wedge has triangle ends with sides 3 centimeters, 4 centimeters and 5 centimeters, and it is 8 centimeters long. It is unfolded flat below. What is the area of all its faces in square centimeters? Find the area of both ends and all three sides. Then add.
Now you try. A box is 6 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 4 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Find the area of the base. Then multiply by the height.

Now you try. You want to know how students at your school get to school. You ask the first 20 kids who get off one bus. Is that a fair sample? Ask, does everyone in the school have the same chance to be picked?

Now you try. You ask 40 students, picked by chance. 10 of them walk to school. Predict how many of all 600 students walk to school. Find the fraction in the sample. Then take that fraction of the whole school.
Now you try. Two classes each grew 5 plants. What is the difference between their mean heights, in inches? Find the mean of each class. Then subtract.
Now you try. This spinner has 10 equal parts. What is the probability of landing on green? Write a fraction or a decimal. Ways it can happen on top. All the equal ways on the bottom.
Now you try. You roll a number cube 60 times. How many times do you expect to roll a 4? Find the chance on one roll. Multiply it by the number of rolls.
Now you try. You flip a coin and roll a number cube. What is the probability of tails and an even number? Fill in the table. Count the pairs you want over all the pairs.
Now you try. Write 3 to the fourth times 3 squared as 3 with one exponent. What is the exponent? Keep the base. Add the exponents.
Now you try. Write 3 to the seventh divided by 3 squared as 3 with one exponent. What is the exponent? Keep the base. Subtract the bottom exponent from the top one.
Now you try. Write 3 squared, all to the fourth, as 3 with one exponent. What is the exponent? Keep the base. Multiply the exponents.
Now you try. What is 3 to the negative 2? Write it as a fraction. Start from a value you know. Divide by the base for each step down.
Now you try. 4,500,000 equals 4 point 5 times 10 to some power. What is the exponent? Make a number from 1 up to 10. Count how many places the point jumps.
Now you try. Zero point zero zero zero seven equals 7 times 10 to the what? What is the exponent? Move the point right to make a number from 1 up to 10. Count the jumps, and make it negative.
Now you try. 3 times 10 to the fifth, times 3 times 10 squared, equals 9 times 10 to the what? What is the exponent? Multiply the front numbers. Add the exponents of 10.
Now you try. What is the square root of 49? Find the number that times itself makes 49.
Now you try. Between which two whole numbers is the square root of 50? Find the perfect square just below 50 and the one just above.
Now you try. The line goes through the points 2, 1 and 4, 7. How steep is it? Find rise divided by run. Count across, then up. Divide the up by the across.
Now you try. A line goes through the points 1, 4 and 5, 16. What is its slope? Subtract the y-values, then the x-values in the same order. Divide.
Now you try. A line has the equation y equals 3 x plus 5. What is its slope? Find the number in front of x.
Now you try. Which point is on the line y equals 2 x minus 1? Put each point’s x into the equation. Does it give that point’s y?
Now you try. Solve 6 x plus 5 equals 3 x plus 20. What is x? Take the smaller x part off both sides. Then solve what is left.
Now you try. How many solutions does 4 x plus 1 equals 4 x plus 7 have? Take the x parts off both sides. Look at what is left.
Now you try. The lines y equals x plus 1 and y equals negative x plus 7 cross at one point. What is the x-value of that point? Find where the lines meet. Check the point in both equations.
Now you try. y equals 3 x and x plus y equals 16. What is x? Put what y equals in place of y. Then solve for x.

Now you try. A family buys 9 tickets. Adult tickets cost 6 dollars and kid tickets cost 3 dollars. They pay 39 dollars. How many adult tickets did they buy? Write one equation for the tickets and one for the dollars. Then solve them together.
Now you try. Is this table a function? Look along the input row. Does any input show up twice with a different output?
Now you try. The rule is output equals 3 times input minus 2. What is the output when the input is 6? Put the input into the rule. Multiply first, then subtract.
Now you try. Is this table linear? Check that x goes up in equal steps. Then find how much y changes each step.
Now you try. Function A is the table. Function B is y equals 3 x plus 10. Which grows faster? Find how much each one goes up for each 1 in x. Compare the two numbers.
Now you try. A skating rink costs 15 dollars to join, plus 8 dollars for each visit. Which rule gives the cost y for x visits? Find the amount that repeats and the amount paid once.

Now you try. The graph shows how many miles Mia is from home. Along the bottom is hours. What is her distance doing between hour 3 and hour 5? Find the two hours along the bottom. Is that piece going up, going down or flat?
Now you try. Point A is at 2, 1. The triangle slides 5 right and 3 up. What is the x-coordinate of A prime? Right and left change x. Up and down change y.
Now you try. Point A is at 3, 2. The triangle flips over the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of A prime? Over the x-axis, the y changes sign. Over the y-axis, the x changes sign.

Now you try. Point A is at 4, 2. The triangle turns a quarter turn counterclockwise around the point 0, 0. What is the x-coordinate of A prime? Swap the two numbers. Then change the sign of the new first number.
Now you try. Point A is at 3, 1. The triangle is stretched from the point 0, 0, multiplying by 2. What is the x-coordinate of A prime? Multiply both coordinates by the stretch number.

Now you try. These two triangles have the same angles. The small one has sides 6, 5 and 3 centimeters. The big one has sides 18, 15 and ? cm. How long is the missing side, in cm? Find the scale factor from a matching pair. Then multiply.
Now you try. A triangle has angles of 40 degrees and 75 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees? Add the two angles you know. Take that away from 180 degrees.
Now you try. A right triangle has short sides of 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters. How long is the long side, in cm? Square the two short sides, add, then undo the square.

Now you try. A right triangle has a long side of 10 centimeters and a short side of 6 centimeters. How long is the other short side, in cm? Square the long side, take away the square of the short side, then undo the square.
Now you try. How far apart are the points 2, 1 and 8, 9, in units? Find how far across and how far up. Those are the legs.
Now you try. A can has a radius of 2 inches and a height of 7 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use pi as three point one four. Find the area of the circle. Then multiply by the height.

Now you try. A cone has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Use pi as three point one four. Find the cylinder with the same bottom and height. Then divide by 3.

Now you try. A ball has a radius of 6 centimeters. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Use pi as three point one four. Multiply the radius by itself three times. Take four thirds of that, then multiply by three point one four.

Now you try. An ice-cream cone has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 8 centimeters. Half a ball of ice cream with a radius of 3 centimeters sits on top. How many cubic centimeters is that in all? Use pi as three point one four. Name the two shapes. Find each one, then add.
Now you try. Each dot is one day at a cafe, the temperature and the cups of hot chocolate sold. What pattern does the plot show? Look at the whole cloud. Does it rise, fall, or neither?
Now you try. A line fits these dots well. It passes through the point 0, 40 and the point 5, 70. What is its slope? Find the rise and the run between the two points. Then divide.
Now you try. The line of best fit for hours studied and test score is y equals 5 x plus 50. Predict the score for 8 hours of studying. Put the hours in place of x. Multiply, then add.
Now you try. How many grade 7 students do not like pizza? Find the row the box is in. Its boxes add up to its total.
Now you try. What percent of grade 7 students like pizza? Ask out of whom? Divide the count by that total, then write it as a percent.

Try a new one. How many kilograms is 3,400 grams?
Try a new one. Each small cube is the same size. How many cubes fill this box?
Try a new one. A box is 3 cubes long, 3 cubes wide and 4 layers high. How many cubes fill it?
Try a new one. A box is 6 in long, 2 in wide and 4 in tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
Try a new one. Two boxes are joined. Box A is 4 in long, 4 in wide and 2 in tall. Box B is 3 in long, 2 in wide and 2 in tall. What is the total volume in cubic inches?
Try a new one. A tray is 3 and one half feet long and 1 and one half feet wide. Each small tile is one half foot on a side. How many square feet is the tray?
Try a new one. Is every rhombus a square?
Try a new one. Each cube is 1 cubic centimeter. What is the volume of this box in cubic centimeters?
Try a new one. What is the second number of point B?
Try a new one. Which point is at 2, 5?
Try a new one. Pattern A, start at 0, add 2. Pattern B, start at 0, add 10. Each number in pattern B is how many times the number above it in pattern A?
Try a new one. Pattern A, start at 0, add 2. Pattern B, start at 0, add 4. Which pair is a dot on this graph?
Try a new one. Point C is at 3 comma 2. Point D is at 3 comma 8. How many units apart are they?
Try a new one. Which place is at 5 comma 4?
Try a new one. A snack mix has 5 pretzels for every 4 crackers. Crackers are 4 out of every how many pieces?
Try a new one. A paint mix uses 3 cans of blue for every 4 cans of white. How many cans of blue go with 16 cans of white?
Try a new one. A car goes 150 miles on 4 gallons of gas. How many miles does it go on one gallon?
Try a new one. A machine fills 120 bottles in 8 minutes. How many bottles does it fill in 5 minutes?
Try a new one. A bakery uses 12 eggs for every 8 cups of flour. How many eggs go with 2 cups of flour?
Try a new one. A bag has 5 red marbles for every 2 blue marbles. There are 42 marbles. How many red marbles are there?
Try a new one. A movie is 150 minutes long. 60 minutes is 1 hour. How many hours long is the movie?
Try a new one. A car drives 220 miles in 4 hours. How many miles per hour is that?
Try a new one. You have one half gallon of juice. Each glass holds one tenth gallon. How many glasses can you fill? Find one half divided by one tenth.
Try a new one. Find one half divided by three fourths.
Try a new one. Find 2 and one half times 1 and one third.
Try a new one. Find 1 and two thirds divided by 2 and one half.
Try a new one. You have 5 cups of rice. Each serving is two thirds cup. How many servings is that?
Try a new one. What is the biggest number that is a factor of both 15 and 25?
Try a new one. What is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 3 and 5?
Try a new one. Take away. Twenty point three minus seven point four five six equals what?
Try a new one. Multiply. Four point three times two point one equals what?
Try a new one. Divide. Six point seven two divided by 4 equals what?
Try a new one. Divide. One point five six divided by zero point one two equals what?
Try a new one. Find 6,048 divided by 32.
Try a new one. Yogurt comes 6 cups for 5 dollars and 10 cents or 4 cups for 3 dollars and 56 cents. Which is the better buy?
Try a new one. This grid has 100 equal squares. What percent of the grid is shaded?
Try a new one. What percent is two fifths?
Try a new one. What is 60 percent of 90?
Try a new one. 7 is 10 percent of what number?
Try a new one. A game costs 80 dollars. It is 25 percent off. What is the sale price, in dollars?
Try a new one. A lamp costs 40 dollars. The sales tax is 5 percent. What is the total, in dollars?
Try a new one. You put 200 dollars in a bank that pays 6 percent a year. How many dollars does the bank pay you in 4 years? Just what the bank pays.
Try a new one. A jar holds n cookies. You eat 2 of them, so n minus 2 cookies are left. How many are left when n equals 9?
Try a new one. Which shows 4 times a number n?
Try a new one. What is 4 n minus 3 when n equals 7?
Try a new one. What is 2 to the fifth?
Try a new one. What is 1 plus 3, all in parentheses, squared, minus 2 times 5?
Try a new one. Which is the same as 5 times x plus 1, all together?
Try a new one. Solve x plus 8 equals 20. What is x?
Try a new one. Solve 6 x equals 54. What is x?
Try a new one. What is the greatest whole number that makes x is less than 9 true?
Try a new one. This shape has a base of 10 feet and a height of 6 feet. Its slanted side is 10 feet. What is its area in square feet?
Try a new one. A triangle has a base of 7 in and a height of 4 in. What is its area in square inches?
Try a new one. An L-shaped rug is drawn below. What is its area in square feet?
Try a new one. This box is 6 in long, 2 in wide and 3 in tall. It is unfolded flat below. How many square inches of paper cover it?
Try a new one. A box is 1 and one half in long, 4 in wide and 2 and one half in tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
Try a new one. Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One is 130 degrees. How many degrees is the other?
Try a new one. Five towers have 2, 8, 4, 9 and 7 cubes. If the cubes are shared fairly, how many cubes are in each tower?
Try a new one. These 7 pumpkins weigh 12, 30, 18, 25, 9, 21 and 14 pounds. What is the middle weight?
Try a new one. These 13 kids marked their shoe size. Which shoe size is the most common?
Try a new one. The low temperatures one week were 41, 36, 45, 50, 38, 43 and 47 degrees Fahrenheit. What is the biggest minus the smallest?
Try a new one. Six test scores are 88, 91, 85, 90, 87 and 30. Which middle describes these scores best?
Try a new one. A team marked how many goals it scored in each game. In how many games did it score 2 or more goals?
Try a new one. This spinner has 6 equal parts. What is the chance of landing on yellow?
Try a new one. A bag has 6 marbles, 5 green and 1 white. You pick one without looking. How likely is green?
Try a new one. A pizza shop charges 11 dollars for 1 pizza, 19 dollars for 2 pizzas and 27 dollars for 3 pizzas. Is the cost proportional to the number of pizzas?
Try a new one. A printer prints 18 pages in 4 minutes, 36 pages in 8 minutes and 54 pages in 12 minutes. What number do you multiply the minutes by to get the pages?
Try a new one. This graph is proportional. It goes through the points zero, zero and four, ten. What is y when x equals 1?
Try a new one. You jog two thirds mile in one sixth hour. How many miles do you jog in one hour?
Try a new one. 4 cups of juice make 10 servings. How many servings do 6 cups make?
Try a new one. A bike cost 80 dollars. On sale it costs 60 dollars. By what percent did the price go down?
Try a new one. A meal costs 36 dollars. You leave an 18 percent tip. What is the total, in dollars?
Try a new one. You guess a trip takes 60 minutes. It really takes 48 minutes. By what percent was your guess off?
Try a new one. What is the opposite of 9?
Try a new one. How far is negative 3 from 0?
Try a new one. Add. negative 6 plus 2 equals what?
Try a new one. Take away. 4 minus negative 3 equals what?
Try a new one. Multiply. 5 times negative 6 equals what?
Try a new one. Divide. 18 divided by negative 3 equals what?
Try a new one. Add. Negative three fourths plus 1 equals what?
Try a new one. It is 3 degrees Celsius in the evening. By morning it is 7 degrees colder. What is the temperature in the morning, in degrees Celsius?
Try a new one. Which is the same as 5 x plus 9 minus 2 x minus 4?
Try a new one. Which is the same as negative 4 times x plus 2, all together?
Try a new one. What is the biggest number you can put outside the parentheses in 10 x plus 15?
Try a new one. Solve 2 x plus 9 equals 3. What is x?
Try a new one. Solve 2 times x minus 5, all together, equals 8. What is x?
Try a new one. What is the greatest whole number that makes 2 x plus 5 is less than 17 true?
Try a new one. Solve negative 4 x is greater than or equal to 24. Which is the answer?
Try a new one. A taxi charges 4 dollars to start, plus 3 dollars for each mile. A ride costs 25 dollars. How many miles long was the ride?
Try a new one. On a plan, 1 centimeter equals 3 meters. A real pool is 21 meters long. How many centimeters long is it on the plan?
Try a new one. A round table has a radius of 4 feet. How far is it around the edge, in feet? Use three point one four.
Try a new one. A round clock face has a diameter of 10 inches. What is its area in square inches? Use pi as three point one four.
Try a new one. Two angles make a straight line. One is 47 degrees. How many degrees is the other?
Try a new one. Two straight lines cross. The top angle is 118 degrees. What is the bottom angle?
Try a new one. Can sticks 6 in, 7 in and 10 in long make a triangle?
Try a new one. A wedge has triangle ends with sides 6 in, 8 in and 10 in, and it is 5 in long. It is unfolded flat below. What is the area of all its faces in square inches?
Try a new one. A box is 7 meters long, 2 meters wide and 5 meters tall. What is its volume in cubic meters?
Try a new one. A town has 2,000 voters. A computer picks 100 of their names by chance to ask about a new park. Is that a fair sample?
Try a new one. At a stadium, 50 fans are picked by chance. 20 of them bought a hat. Predict how many of all 2,000 fans bought a hat.
Try a new one. Two teams of 4 runners ran a lap. Their times are in seconds. What is the difference between the two mean times?
Try a new one. This spinner has 5 equal parts. What is the probability of landing on red? Write a fraction or a decimal.
Try a new one. A spinner has 4 equal parts, and 1 part is red. You spin it 80 times. How many times do you expect red?
Try a new one. You spin a spinner with 3 equal parts, red, blue and green, and flip a coin. What is the probability of blue and heads?
Try a new one. Write 7 to the fifth times 7 cubed as 7 with one exponent. What is the exponent?
Try a new one. Write 5 to the ninth divided by 5 cubed as 5 with one exponent. What is the exponent?
Try a new one. Write 7 to the fifth, all squared, as 7 with one exponent. What is the exponent?
Try a new one. What is 4 to the negative 2? Write it as a fraction.
Try a new one. 72,000,000 equals 7 point 2 times 10 to some power. What is the exponent?
Try a new one. Zero point zero zero zero zero six one equals six point one times 10 to the what? What is the exponent?
Try a new one. 2 times 10 to the sixth, times 4 times 10 cubed, equals 8 times 10 to the what? What is the exponent?
Try a new one. What is the square root of 64?
Try a new one. Between which two whole numbers is the square root of 30?
Try a new one. The line goes through the points 1, 3 and 5, 6. How steep is it? Find rise divided by run.
Try a new one. A line goes through the points 1, 9 and 4, 3. What is its slope?
Try a new one. A line has the equation y equals negative 2 x plus 7. Where does it cross the y-axis? Give the y-value.
Try a new one. What is y on the line y equals 3 x plus 2 when x equals 4?
Try a new one. Solve 2 x plus 12 equals 5 x plus 3. What is x?
Try a new one. How many solutions does 3 times x plus 2, all together, equal 3 x plus 6 have?
Try a new one. The lines y equals 2 x and y equals x plus 3 cross at one point. What is the y-value of that point?
Try a new one. y equals x plus 2 and x plus y equals 10. What is y?
Try a new one. Phone Plan A costs 20 dollars to start plus 5 dollars a month. Plan B costs 8 dollars to start plus 7 dollars a month. After how many months do they cost the same?
Try a new one. Is this table a function?
Try a new one. f of x equals 2 x plus 5. What is f of 7?
Try a new one. In this table x goes 1, 2, 3, 4 and y goes 1, 4, 9, 16. Is it linear?
Try a new one. Function A is y equals 2 x plus 9. Function B is the table. Which grows faster?
Try a new one. A tree is 4 feet tall and grows 2 feet each year. Which rule gives its height y after x years?
Try a new one. The graph shows how many miles Jon is from home. What is his distance doing between hour 6 and hour 9?
Try a new one. Point B is at 6, 5. The triangle slides 4 left and 2 down. What is the y-coordinate of B prime?
Try a new one. Point B is at 4, negative 3. The triangle flips over the y-axis. What is the x-coordinate of B prime?
Try a new one. Point B is at 3, negative 5. The triangle makes a half turn around the point 0, 0. What is the y-coordinate of B prime?
Try a new one. Point B is at 2, 4. The triangle is stretched from the point 0, 0, multiplying by 3. What is the y-coordinate of B prime?
Try a new one. These two triangles have the same angles. The small one has sides 8, 6 and 4 in. The big one has sides 32, ? and 16 in. How long is the missing side, in inches?
Try a new one. A triangle has angles of 35 degrees and 90 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
Try a new one. A right triangle has short sides of 5 meters and 12 meters. How long is the long side, in meters?
Try a new one. A right triangle has a long side of 13 feet and a short side of 12 feet. How long is the other short side, in feet?
Try a new one. How far apart are the points 1, 2 and 6, 14, in units?
Try a new one. A glass is 6 centimeters across and 10 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Use pi as three point one four.
Try a new one. A cone has a radius of 6 inches and a height of 2 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use pi as three point one four.
Try a new one. A ball is 9 inches across. What is its volume in cubic inches? Use pi as three point one four.
Try a new one. A can has a radius of 2 inches and a height of 6 inches. A ball has a radius of 3 inches. Which holds more? Use pi as three point one four.
Try a new one. Each dot is one of 12 students, the month they were born and their math score. What pattern does the plot show?
Try a new one. A line fits the dots for weeks and plant height in centimeters. It passes through the point 2, 10 and the point 6, 30. What is its slope?
Try a new one. The line of best fit for weeks and plant height in cm is y equals 2 x plus 4. Predict the height at 9 weeks.
Try a new one. How many girls have no pet?
Try a new one. Of the students who have a pet, what fraction are girls? Write it as a fraction.

text: You counted the rows and one row, then multiplied. That is the whole trick.
You turned the rows around and the total stayed the same. That is the whole trick.
You jumped a whole group at a time. Counting by jumps is multiplying.
You added the same group every jump. That is the whole trick.
You shared the total fairly. That is division.
You made groups of the same size and counted them. Check it, 3 packs of 5 is 15.
You made groups of the same size and counted them. Check it, 5 cars with 4 wheels each is 20.
You used a times fact to find the missing number. That is the whole trick.
You found the hour, then counted by 5s.
You found the hour, then counted by 5s to 40.
You counted by 5s, then by 1s, to the exact minute.
You counted by 5s, then by 1s, to read 5 38.
You jumped from the start to the end and added up the jumps.
You jumped from 12 oh 5 to 12 50 and added up 45 minutes.
You found what one mark is worth and counted to the needle.
You counted the marks and found the cat weighs 7 kilograms.
You found what one mark is worth and counted up to the top.
You counted up the marks and found 3 liters.
You found the two tens and picked the closer one.
You found that 78 is closer to 80.
You found the two hundreds and picked the closer one.
You found that 680 is closer to 700.
You added the ones first and traded 10 ones for a ten.
You traded 10 ones for 1 ten and found 316 plus 259 equals 575.
You broke a ten when there were not enough ones.
You broke a ten and found 572 minus 336 equals 236.
You saw that empty plates hold no cookies, however many plates there are.
You saw that 9 empty plates still hold no cookies.
You saw that 1 in each group keeps the number the same.
You saw that 1 plate of 9 cookies is just 9 cookies.
You used a 5s fact you know, then added one more group.
You found 5 rows of 5, then added one more row of 5.
You broke 7 groups into 5s and 2s, two facts you know.
You split 7 days into 5 days and 2 days, then added the parts.
You found 4 groups, then doubled it to get 8 groups.
You found 4 packs of 5, then doubled it.
You used an easy 10s fact, then took one group away.
You found 10 boxes of 6, then took one box of 6 away.
You broke a big fact into two smaller facts and added them.
You broke 8 times 6 into two smaller facts and added them.
You counted the tens, then turned the tens into a number.
You counted the tens, then wrote them as 80.
You answered the hidden question first, then the real one.
You found how many crayons Leo bought, then took away the 6 he lost.
You counted every tile once, with no gaps and no overlaps.
You counted every tile once and found 12 square feet.
You multiplied the rows by the tiles in a row. That is the area.
You multiplied 2 rows by 5 tiles in a row to find the area.
You broke a hard fact into two easy pieces and added them.
You cut the rug after 5 tiles and added the two pieces to get 28.
You cut the L into two rectangles, found each area, and added.
You cut the room into two rectangles and added them to get 16 square feet.
You checked the size of every piece before you said fair.
You checked that all 6 pieces were the same size.
You counted the equal pieces for the bottom and the shaded piece for the top.
You found 1 piece out of 3 equal pieces.
You counted all the pieces for the bottom and your pieces for the top.
You found 3 pieces out of 8 equal pieces.
You counted the equal jumps in the whole, then the jumps to the dot.
You counted 3 equal jumps in the whole, then the jumps to the dot.
You saw that two thirds and four sixths cover the same amount.
You saw that one fourth and two eighths cover the same amount.
You saw that all 6 of the 6 pieces make 1 whole.
You saw that all 3 pieces make 1 whole sandwich.
You compared the top numbers because the pieces were the same size.
You compared 3 pieces and 1 piece of the same size.
You took the same number of pieces and picked the bigger pieces.
You took 3 pieces from each and picked the bigger pieces.
You counted each row by 2s, then found how many more.
You counted each row by 2s and added them all.
